chapterBreakdown.direct:
Chapter 4 centers on prompts. Fogg's point is that a behavior can be well chosen and easy enough and still fail because no event reliably initiates it. That is why the chapter focuses on anchor prompts and the power of after.

An after prompt ties the new tiny behavior to something that already happens. That matters because the existing routine provides a stable place in the sequence. After brushing teeth, floss one tooth. After opening the laptop, check the first task. After class ends, review one card. The method reduces dependence on memory and vague intention by giving the habit a real starting line.

The chapter is careful not to flatten all prompts into equal value. A good prompt fits the timing and context of the day. A bad one appears when attention is elsewhere, when the routine is rushed, or when the anchor itself is unreliable. Then the prompt becomes background noise instead of ignition.

The deeper lesson is that behavior design includes when the action begins, not only what the action is. Prompts give the habit a time and place to enter reality. That makes them a full design lever, not a decorative reminder trick.
chapterBreakdown.competitive:
Chapter 4 fixes a simple but expensive problem: lots of habits fail because nothing actually fires them. The plan exists. The behavior is easy enough. The desire is there. But the routine still dies because the trigger is vague. Fogg's answer is the power of after.

Anchor prompts work because they recruit an existing sequence instead of depending on memory alone. After I brush my teeth. After I open my laptop. After class ends. The old routine becomes the launch rail for the new behavior. That is stronger than hoping the right thought arrives at the right time.

The chapter also sharpens the idea by refusing to treat every reminder as good design. Timing matters. Context matters. A trigger that lands in a chaotic or unstable moment often becomes noise. A strong anchor is ordinary, visible, and repeatable enough to start the behavior cleanly.

That is why prompts deserve their own chapter. Motivation and ability can make behavior possible, but prompts make behavior start. If you ignore ignition, you keep asking intention to do a job that sequence should do better.

chapterBreakdown.gentle:
Sofia wants to review one note card after class, and somehow the habit keeps evaporating between the classroom door and the hallway chatter. Chapter 4 says that is not mysterious. A behavior can be well matched and easy and still fail if nothing starts it. BJ Fogg calls that missing event the prompt.

That is why the chapter centers on the power of after. Instead of asking memory to produce the habit at the perfect moment, tie the tiny behavior to something that already happens. After I brush my teeth, I floss one tooth. After I open my laptop, I check the list. After class ends, I review one card. The value is not only the phrase. The value is the sequence. An existing routine creates a cleaner starting line than intention floating by itself.

The chapter also refuses to treat prompts as generic reminders. A strong prompt does not merely exist. It fits. It appears when the environment can actually support the tiny behavior. If it lands in a rushed, unstable, or emotionally noisy moment, the new habit can feel brittle. That is why the chapter respects the trailing edge of a real routine. The old action can hand the new action a usable opening if the handoff is natural enough.

This makes the method more exact than it first sounds. Motivation may make the habit desirable. Ease may make it possible. The prompt makes it begin. If initiation is weak, the rest of the design never gets a fair test. That is the chapter's deeper claim: behavior design includes timing and sequence, not just desire and difficulty.

The chapter's live tension is fit. Not every old routine deserves to become an anchor. Some are too rushed, too unstable, or too loaded with conflict. A bad anchor can turn prompting into noise. So the real discipline is not only to add a cue. It is to choose a cue that belongs naturally enough to the day that the handoff feels clean instead of forced. That is what makes after powerful rather than merely clever.
chapterBreakdown.direct:
Chapter 4 focuses on prompts because a behavior can be wanted and easy and still fail if nothing reliably initiates it. Fogg's answer is not to ask the reader to remember harder. It is to design initiation through anchor prompts and the power of after.

An after prompt attaches the tiny behavior to something that already happens. That matters because the existing routine provides a stable place in the sequence. The new behavior no longer depends on a free-floating intention. It inherits time and context from the anchor action.

The chapter is stronger when it distinguishes prompts from reminders in general. A useful prompt is not just visible. It is well placed. If it lands in a rushed transition or on top of an unstable routine, it may become noise or friction instead of ignition. A good anchor is ordinary enough to repeat and clear enough to notice.

This is why prompting deserves to stand beside motivation and ability as a full design lever. Motivation can make action attractive. Ease can make it feasible. Prompting makes it start. When initiation keeps failing, the problem may be sequence more than desire.

The limit is that anchor choice can be lazy. Readers can assume any existing routine will work and then wonder why the new habit feels brittle. The chapter's harder lesson is that fit governs prompts too. A strong cue belongs to the actual flow of the day instead of being stapled onto it artificially.
chapterBreakdown.competitive:
Chapter 4 fixes an initiation problem. Lots of habits fail because nothing cleanly fires them. The behavior is small enough. The desire is there. The routine still dies because sequence was left vague. Fogg solves that with prompts and the power of after.

The logic is straightforward. Borrow an old routine to launch the new one. After brushing. After opening the laptop. After class ends. The existing action becomes a launch rail, which is far stronger than asking memory or motivation to improvise the start every time.

The chapter gets sharper when it rejects the idea that any reminder counts as good design. Trigger quality depends on placement. A cue dropped into a noisy, unstable, or rushed moment often turns into background clutter. A strong anchor is repeatable enough to be trusted and ordinary enough to be seen without strain.

That is why prompts matter as much as they do. Motivation does not start behavior by itself. Ease does not start behavior by itself. Sequence starts behavior. If ignition is weak, the rest of the system never gets a fair chance.

The harder read is that after only works when the handoff is real. Readers who staple a tiny behavior onto a bad anchor will call the method weak when the design is the weak part. The chapter's edge is not adding more cues. It is choosing a cue that belongs to the day strongly enough to start the action cleanly.
